Grant all privileges on all tables in the public schema to the public role

Here is the SQL command to grant all privileges on all tables in the `public` schema to the `public` role:

```sql
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO PUBLIC;
```

### Breakdown

| Component | Description |
|---|---|
| `ALL PRIVILEGES` | Grants all applicable privileges (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER) |
| `ALL TABLES` | Applies to all **existing** tables in the specified schema |
| `IN SCHEMA public` | Targets the `public` schema |
| `TO PUBLIC` | Grants to the special `PUBLIC` role, meaning **all users/roles** |

### ⚠️ Important Notes

- This only applies to **existing tables** at the time the command is run. For future tables, you need to set default privileges:
```sql
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLES TO PUBLIC;
```
- Granting to `PUBLIC` means **every user** in the database will have these privileges, which can be a **security risk**. Consider granting to a specific role instead:
```sql
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO your_role;
```
- To **revoke** these privileges later:
```sql
REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
```
